audit.whatIsWrong: diff says EVEN, tone is the orange TRICKY colour, diffRating says 7/10 and both difficulty lines say 'Tricky matchup' — on a lane the packet scores 54.38% across 160 games. The full layer also calls Irelia 'he' and 'his' in eight places.
audit.why: A 54% lane over 160 games is not a 7/10, and three different grades on one page make all of them worthless. EVEN with a 6/10 is the read that matches both the win rate and the page's own prose.
audit.corrected: Tone moved to the even colour, diffRating to 6/10, and both difficulty lines rewritten to Even. Pronouns fixed to her throughout the full layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flawless Duet is named the clock on six lines with no number, and no other Irelia cooldown appears anywhere.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, Bladesurge 10/9/8/7/6s and refreshes on a Marked target or a kill, Defiant Dance 20/18/16/14/12s and Vanguard's Edge 125/105/85s. Your Miasma is 24s, so you get one grounding per two of her stun setups — which is why you save it for the Bladesurge, not the poke.
audit.corrected: 16s, 10s, 20s, 125s and your own 24s written into the cooldown block, the trigger card, the wants list and the mid text, with the Bladesurge reset condition stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two claims are false and they run through five slots. The page says Miasma 'also locks her E dash' and that 'she has to place a blade then dash to it' — Flawless Duet is not a dash. And it says twice that Defiant Dance's damage reduction eats or blanks your burst.
audit.why: Riot's Flawless Duet text: 'Irelia sends out two blades which converge on each other. Enemies caught in between are damaged, stunned and Marked.' There is no dash in it — the counterplay is not standing on the line between the blades, which is different advice entirely. And Defiant Dance says 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge': your entire kit is magic, so her W reduces nothing you do. Telling a Cassiopeia to fear that window costs her the best trade in the lane.
audit.corrected: The phantom E dash removed everywhere and replaced with the converging-blades geometry; Defiant Dance restated as physical-only so you trade straight through it. Grounding is now sold against Bladesurge alone.

edits.before: This is your window. Do not fear Defiant Dance — it reduces physical damage only, and every point of yours is magic. At 6, hold Petrifying Gaze for her all-in: face her as she dashes in and the stun ends it.

edits.before: The matchup flips here if she got going. A fed Irelia with Trinity Force and resist items becomes a front-to-back monster — her W (Defiant Dance) damage-reduction blanks your burst windows and her passive (Ionian Fervor) on-hits plus lifesteal sustain her through your poison, while you stay squishy with no resistances and short range. Your job is to have won lane already: snowball your level 4-to-first-item dominance into objectives and end before her item spike. If it goes long, never get caught alone — group, save W to ground her engage in fights, and let your frontline soak her dive while you DPS from max range.

Defiant Dance is not the problem: it cuts physical damage only, and every point of yours is magic.
